analysis: The code snippet defines a method that converts an Iterator to a string. It first checks if the iterator has any elements via hasNext(). If not, it returns "[]" immediately, avoiding any call to next(). If the iterator has elements, it calls next() once after the check, then enters a while loop that repeatedly checks hasNext() before each subsequent next() call. The only exception declared in next()'s documentation is NoSuchElementException, which occurs if hasNext() returns false. Since every call to next() is preceded by a hasNext() check that ensures at least one element exists, NoSuchElementException is fully avoided in this context.
remark: All calls to iterator.next() are guarded by iterator.hasNext() checks, so NoSuchElementException cannot occur. No other exceptions are declared for next().
